correctness.rationale: An antipodal pair has disjoint closed neighborhoods covering all twelve vertices. Four-sets comprising the antipodes and one neighbor each are paired-dominating. No adjacent two-set dominates. The finite lemma enumerates all 30 host edges against all disjoint second edges, obtaining exactly nine successful completions per edge and finding an antipodal pair in every completion. A direct count with double-antipodal overlap yields 135 four-sets and a 60/60/15 structural split. Exact transition testing of all 32 possible directed one-token replacements per state, and BFS from each of 135 roots, verifies the reconfiguration cardinalities and sharp self-centered diameters. Two standalone programs using unrelated geometric and combinatorial constructions agree on all data.

value.rationale: This is a complete geometric classification of optimal paired guard placements on a canonical polyhedral graph. It identifies the antipodal involution as a necessary condition, then gives exact costs and connectivity of two distinct relocation models under the backup-matching constraint. Both graphs are self-centered but have different diameters, so the exact mobility information is not determined by the scalar paired-domination number. The natural symmetry, complete classification and sharp metrics are independently motivated; the calculation is finite but exhausts the precise mathematical object.
